newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-PORTUGAL NEARLY SPRING GERMAN SURPRISE AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTUGAL NEARLY SPRING GERMAN SURPRISE AGAIN.

text.p: Portugal, the only side to beat Germany in a World Cup qualifier, nearly did it again on Saturday but had to settle finally for a spirited 0-0 draw.
The Portuguese, who played at the start as if believing history never repeated itself, grew in confidence in the second half and were only denied by a fine piece of goalkeeping by Andreas Koepke.

Benfica striker Joao Vieira Pinto dribbled brilliantly across the face of the area leaving a trail of German defenders in his wake before cutting into the box, but Koepke managed to deflect his shot round the post.
It was the clearest chance of a tight game in which the Germans, the reigning European champions, dominated the early exchanges but had few clear opportunities to score.

The result leaves Portugal on top of European qualifying group nine with eight points from five games, with Germany in third on five points, a point behind Ukraine in second. But the Germans and Ukraine have played two fewer games than Portugal.
"In the second half we played well. We saw that the Germans were tiring and that was when the chances came," Portuguese coach Artur Jorge told journalists.
Germany, playing in their usual measured and controlled style, pushed forward from the start and had a number of half-chances in the opening 20 minutes.
Juergen Klinsmann, who had a quiet match, broke free down the right and sent over a delicate chip to Fredi Bobic but the Stuttgart's header was bundled away for a corner.
The Germans could probably feel aggrieved that Hungarian referee Sandor Puhl did not award them a penalty when defender Carlos Secretario appeared to bring down Bobic in the box.
There was little however in the first half to inspire the 50,000 crowd in Lisbon's Stadium of Light who had come to see Portugal repeat their feat of 1985 when they beat Germany 1-0 away.
Portugal stepped up the pace after the break and Fiorentina midfielder Rui Costa had a chance to open the scoring in the 48th minute but his shot lacked power.
At the other end, keeper Vitor Baia was forced to make a diving save to his right when Bobic nearly lobbed him with a header from a centre by Bayern Munich wingback Christian Ziege.
Germany came to Portugal without three of their first team regulars due to injury and were probably relieved to come away with a point at the end.
"I am happy with the result," German coach Berti Vogts said. We had our chances in the first half but the second half was more exciting and Portugal showed that they are a good side."

Portugal: 1-Vitor Baia, 2-Carlos Secretario, 5-Fernando Couto, 6-Helder Cristovao, 3-Dimas Teixeira, 11-Paulinho Santos, 4-Oceano Cruz, 7-Luis Figo, 10-Rui Costa, 9-Rui Barros (17-Jorge Cadete 76), 8-Joao Vieira Pinto.

Germany: 1-Andreas Koepke, 6-Matthias Sammer, 4-Juergen Kohler, 2-Stefan Reuter, 8-Markus Babbel (15-Michael Tarnat 85), 5-Dieter Eilts, 3-Christian Ziege, 10-Mario Basler (13-Ulf Kirsten 70), 7-Andreas Moeller, 11-Fredi Bobic, 9-Juergen Klinsmann.
